decisions.label: documented-and-verifiable
decisions.evidence_note: README specifies CodaLab submission format {test_id: label} with 0/1 labels and details of tokenized/preprocessed JSON formats. QqpProcessor in run_BERT.py specifies TSV columns (ids, column_types, text_a, text_b, label) for train/dev/test examples.

decisions.label: documented-and-verifiable
decisions.evidence_note: run_BERT.py defines simple_accuracy as mean of (preds == labels), acc_and_f1 combining accuracy and sklearn f1_score, and pearson_and_spearman using scipy; compute_metrics for task 'qqp' returns acc_and_f1.

decisions.label: partially-documented
decisions.evidence_note: Core evaluation utilities (data processing, feature conversion, metric functions) are implemented in run_BERT.py. However, main() is truncated, so the full end-to-end evaluation script (loading predictions, invoking metrics, reporting results) cannot be fully reconstructed from the visible snippet.

decisions.label: not-documented
decisions.evidence_note: README lists benchmark scores but does not state how official rankings are decided, how multiple runs/checkpoints are handled, or how ties are broken. Code defines metrics but no policy for ranking systems or resolving equal scores is described.

decisions.label: documented-and-verifiable
decisions.evidence_note: simple_accuracy computes the aggregate score as the mean over elementwise equality between prediction and label arrays. compute_metrics for the 'qqp' task returns acc_and_f1, which aggregates accuracy and F1. The mapping from per-example predictions to these aggregate metrics is explicit.

decisions.label: not-documented
decisions.evidence_note: README and run_BERT.py describe formats and logging of example inputs but do not provide any concrete example prediction files, trajectories, or end-to-end sample outputs demonstrating model predictions alongside scores.
